newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Tigon claws back some gains.
newsitem.headline: Tigon claws back some gains.

text.p: Shares in South African electronics distributor and financial services group Tigon Ltd clawed back some of their enorm/us recent losses on Wednesday, dealers said.
Volumes were light with only 88,200 shares changing hands as some buying crept into the bombed-out stock.

The firm has suffered heavily after the Johannesburg Stock Exchange suspended the firm's shares over the accounting of its 1996 financial results. Tigon then said 17.9 million rand, or 54 percent of its income for the period, was based on a fee that was not due to be received until October. The suspension on the firm's shares was then lifted.
"Some guys are willing to take a chance now that things are becoming clearer, but a lot of people got their fingers burnt," one dealer said.
Tigon shares, which were trading as high as 18.80 rand this April, were up 60 cents to 365 cents by 0940 GMT.
They hit a year low of 300 rand on Tuesday.
